source_hebrew: Westminster Leningrad Codex (pointed text via Sefaria)

2:22.hebrew: חִדְלוּ לָכֶם מִן־הָאָדָם אֲשֶׁר נְשָׁמָה בְּאַפּוֹ כִּי־בַמֶּה נֶחְשָׁב הוּא׃
2:22.english: Turn away from mortals, whose breath is in their nostrils. For what do they amount to?
2:22.editorial_note: The Hebrew uses a generic singular for human beings.

56:12.hebrew: אֵתָיוּ אֶקְחָה־יַיִן וְנִסְבְּאָה שֵׁכָר וְהָיָה כָזֶה יוֹם מָחָר גָּדוֹל יֶתֶר מְאֹד׃
56:12.english: “Come, I’ll get wine, and we’ll drink our fill of strong drink. Tomorrow will be like today, only far more abundant.”

scope: Additional readings keyed by Masoretic reference, separate from the Parallel Reader’s aligned rows. Entries with staging links document the earlier staging capture. New editorial readings were prepared in the GitHub archive.
